To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
selection for components of efficient growth in pigs can be effective, and that lean growth rate is the most effective selection criterion.

selection for LGA, which is the lean growth rate in a pig, is the most effective selection objective for both LGA and lean food conversion (the food conversion of the lean component of the body), without a reduction in food intake.

(1) selection on lean food conversion ratio is as effective as selection on lean growth rate for improving the lean food conversion ratio; (2) selection on lean growth is more effective than selection on lean food intake for improving lean food conversion ratio, without reducing lean food intake.
In summary, our research is concerned with
selection for lean growth efficiency in pigs.
the genetic improvement of components of lean growth rate in swine.
improving lean growth efficiency in pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selection of LFC has the same effect on LFC as selection on LGA, but with a negative effect on DFI, while selection on LGA is more efficient than selection on LFC in terms of LGA and DFi.
selection on LGA is the most effective way to improve both LGA and the LFC, without affecting DFI.
selection for LGA is the best way to improve lean food conversion, and that it is also a good way of improving LGA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
selection on LGA has been more successful than selection on LFC in improving LGA, LCF and DFI, and that selection on DFI has not been successful in improving LGA and LCF.
selection for LGA is a more effective selection criterion than LFC for improving both LFC and DFi.
the selection for LGA is the best strategy to improve LFC and DFC simultaneously.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LGA selection objective is an effective tool for improving both LFC and DFC.

the selection for components of efficient growth rate in pigs has identified lean growth rate as the most effective selection objective for both lean growth rate and lean food conversion, without a reduction of food intake.
selection on lean growth rate with a high feed intake is more efficient than selection on food conversion ratio in pigs.
